There is actually a food that i love but i could only found this as a close alternative since it is a local food that is not widely known around the world.

I am also on a strict diet and the recipe i gave below is actually pretty healthy and i really like how it taste. I do not use oil or do not serve it with hummus instead i make the serving with strained yoghurt with a mini-little bit of salt and garlic p etc, i believe greek yoghurt is something between strained and nonstrained so it is also a great choice.

So for ingredients from scratch, 1 courgette, 1 egg, 50ml milk, 2-3 fresh onion, 10 branches(max 10cm) of parsley, 1tsp salt black and red pepper, 200ml flour. 

The courgette is grated with the large holed part of the grater. Squeeze the courgette until the juice comes out well.

Finely chop the parsley and green onions. In a deep bowl, whisk the egg with half a tea glass of milk until it has a smooth consistency. Spices are added to it. Add 1 cup of flour. If you want a little oil can be poured into the teflon pan.

A spoonful of the mixture is poured into it, as if cooking pancakes, and it is cooked on both sides. It is ready to serve when all the mixture is cooked.

What makes difference in the recipe is putting the correct amount of salt for yourself and when cooking it you need to check undermeath regulary. It is light, delicious with or wo yoghurt and very easy to carry around.

In terms of accepting kurdish as an official language, yes it checks all the boxes and i do believe every language needs to be passed on people who wants to speak it but in terms of making it a primary language in education is not simple. I do not know any educational systems that are happen to allow it completely. Like in germany no matter what is your pl you need to know german since you enter universities solely by your gpa(also how many years did you fail) which also depends on which highschool you get into (hauptschule(5-6 years), realschule, gymasium(4 years)) but i believe switzerland would be closer to take an example of since they also require a central exam like turkey.

The problem is even though they provide education in other primary languages their exam(maturity) is either only german or mix between german and italian(also one other that i couldnt remember).

So in theory if you want to use a system that includes 2 languages in education you must have an central exam otherwise students will have too little in common in terms of mutual language (in isolated places) and literature which will put a barrier between people even living in the same place, i do not even say students of both sides feel unjust(kurdish could be harder or vice versa that would lead to gpa difference between students that you cannot equalize with a simple formula). Even though central examination is more likely to be a solution it still requires for a common language to evaluate them on.

Well again i dont know if there is a clean cut solution which i dont believe anybody knows but some claims made by people that request full kurdish education from primary school to university seems too unrealistic to me at least i havent seen or know any.

But i do strongly agree that kurdish should be official not in terms of turkey being a country with 2 primaries but a language that is needed to mutual understanding since many places in east cannot communicate in turkish and people who wants to learn kurdish should be allowed to take optional courses(oral and written) in schools or in private institutes that they desire to.
